# PR #256 final performance verdict

Head: d94fa60ff4a214f6101987a64939e1e361d17c85
Reviewed delta: 695aae4a4033941c44dfead656ef070febf9fef9..d94fa60ff4a214f6101987a64939e1e361d17c85
Result: PASS WITH NOTES. Final round under C34. No normal-use runtime cost breach in the delta and no unresolved performance blocker from round 1. Post-deploy measurement remains owed by PERFORMANCE ONLY.

## Findings disposition

R256-001 guard scoring is corrected: stats() now reads old_guard/new_guard, and warnings count separately from silent allows and refusals. The committed final-head audit smoke over the original seven-day window returned 14620 delivered, 13404 paired, 9402 decided. Independent aggregation found zero new_guard row mismatches and zero guard-total mismatches. Guard totals: silent cold 970 -> 710 (large 265 -> 5), warm refused-or-warned 4 -> 56, refused 124 -> 124, warned 0 -> 312. The corrected guard numbers and all four policy replay rows agree with the corrected note and PR body.

Important interpretation: Warn still ALLOWS 265 large actual-cold deliveries, 260 with warnings. It does not prevent those cache rewrites. Four actually-warm deliveries would still be refused, 52 newly warned, rather than 56 refused. Do not convert the former Refuse policy's avoided-wake estimate into shipped Warn savings. This remains a reconstructed replay, not an observed after-deploy false-refusal rate.

A bounded diagnostic caveat remains: cache_old_* uses old_warm, the fixed-hour predicate, not old_cache, the old TTL-based CACHE view. My verification accepts the guard_* and replay metrics; it does not certify cache_old_* as the former CACHE column's error rate. Correctness disposition stays with the reviewer; no cost block follows from this label issue.

## Delta cost

`PastTtl` adds a constant-time branch and optional saturating percentage arithmetic, not a read, launch, timer, task or loop. Default Warn formats the already-existing warning string for eligible sends. TTL still comes from the same existing incremental status read. The enum/switch itself carries no heap allocation. No new daemon launch site requires a spawn-counter update.

Round-1 qualification is narrowed for the actual default: Warn makes the idle projection Warn, not Cold, between TTL and the hour; `http/cold_wake.rs` therefore no longer enters the stale-working activity lookup/pane-probe branch solely for that short-TTL range. RefuseAt can re-enable that conditional existing branch. Existing PA 60-second cadence, descriptor-copy cost per admitted seat read, sized-list O(seats) work and retained status cursors/misses are unchanged in this delta. New test subprocesses are two explicit Python runs per test-file execution in CI, not production work.

Nudge clarification: `idle_nudge.rs:362-363` admits only Clear|Busy, so Warn still spares an idle-nudge wake. My interim generic 'Warn/allow nudge' message was incorrect for that path. The separately opted-in watchdog path, `pa_watchdog.rs:939`, gates on refusal and can allow Warn; these are distinct paths. FYI flush/revive cache_known evidence requirements are unchanged.

Audit replay adds four O(decided rows) in-memory policy passes and a printed comparison; no additional SQLite query, transcript opening or daemon request. Final-head on-demand smoke `/usr/bin/time -lp just cache-ttl-audit /tmp/f214/fr-all --json /tmp/f214/performance-256-d94fa60.json` exited 0: 9.85s wall, 4.05s user, 1.42s system, maximum RSS187613184B, swaps0. This is not a controlled speed comparison with round 1's 12.18s/175128576B run. The same full-store/full-transcript scan shape remains: three spine scans, about3.475GB of Copilot logs plus93.60MB report calls in the prior measured input set. Keep it on demand, not on a timer.
